clue.text: Fit to grasp point of gap

indicators.note: to grasp means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: fit means in good shape, i.e. in trim
E, east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Something tailored to cover a single feature of a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' is the two-word phrase IN TRIM, which is then split to take E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An interim is an intervening period, a gap between two events or arrangements.

clue.text: Cop for hot dog

parts.note: hot means fashionable, which is also in
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A policeman swaps places with a frankfurter.
explanation.definitionFit: To cop something, such as a fine or the blame, is informal for to suffer it.

clue.text: Short Sri Lankan star engulfed by disaster

indicators.note: engulfed by means the earlier piece sits inside the later one
short means the last letter is lopped off

parts.note: a Tamil is a member of a people of Sri Lanka
the sun is a star

explanation.surface: A diminutive Sri Lankan celebrity overwhelmed by catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge sea wave and, by extension, any overwhelming catastrophe.

clue.text: Clothes a capital

parts.note: rig is an informal word for an outfit

explanation.surface: Dressing up a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Riga is the capital of Latvia.

clue.text: Drug (speed?) bringing partner round, one choked by gas

indicators.note: choked by means the earlier pieces are held inside the later one

parts.note: methane is a gas
mph, miles per hour, measures speed

indicators.note: round means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: a mate is a partner
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A stimulant, perhaps speed, brings a partner round when gassed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speed?' looks like the definition in brackets, but it is MPH.
explanation.definitionFit: Methamphetamine is a synthetic stimulant drug, also called crystal meth.

clue.text: Come to point about pious character's drinks dispenser

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: to taper is to narrow to a point
ST, saint, abbreviates a holy person

explanation.surface: A devout figure arrives at the point of being a barman.
explanation.definitionFit: Old word for a barman or person who draws beer from the tap.

clue.text: Deflate daughter's alternative band

indicators.note: alternative says another order of these letters is wanted

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter, so only the word daughter itself is fodder

explanation.surface: A girl's indie group lets the air out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grateful Dead were an American rock group formed in 1965.

clue.text: Recycled document, white as can be, infested by gremlins

indicators.note: infested by means the first piece has the second within it

parts.note: palest is as white as possible
imps are mischievous sprites, as gremlins are

explanation.surface: A recycled paper, bleached white, is overrun with gremlins.
explanation.definitionFit: A palimpsest is a manuscript scraped clean and written over again, so a reused document.

clue.text: Centre (that of Siena?) redesigned by Roman playwright

indicators.note: redesigned means the letters are put in a new arrangement
that of refers back to centre, so the middle letter of Siena is taken

explanation.surface: A Sienese centre remodelled by a classical dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: Terence was a comic dramatist of ancient Rome.

clue.text: Playground adjoining right-winger's ecclesiastical home

parts.note: REC is short for recreation ground, a park
a Tory is a member of the UK's right-wing Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A park next to a Conservative's house of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: A rectory is the house of a rector, a parish clergyman.

clue.text: Embedded impulse to stew peeled vegetable

parts.note: an impulse is an URGE; put to bed it lies in a COT, so the urge sits inside COT

indicators.note: peeled means the outer letters of stew are stripped off, keeping its core

explanation.surface: An ingrained compulsion to cook a skinned vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Embedded' carries the bed itself: URGE placed in COT (a child's bed) gives CO-URGE-T; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A courgette is a small marrow, called zucchini in America, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Unusually rich part of song

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An unusually rich passage in a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric is a short songlike poem, or the words of a song.

clue.text: Bring up what gets brought up?

definitions.meaning: to bring up children is to raise them
one brings up the back end of a procession

explanation.definitionFit: To rear is to raise; the rear is the back, which someone 'brings up' in a procession.

clue.text: City's a study in artificial stone

indicators.note: in means the second piece sits inside the first
artificial means the letters of stone are made into something unnatural

parts.note: to cram is to study hard before an exam

explanation.surface: A city is a piece of research into man-made stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City's' looks like a possessive, but the 's is just 'is' linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacramento is the state capital of California.

clue.text: Art endeavouring to encapsulate no-good underwear?

indicators.note: to encapsulate means the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: in old English 'thou art endeavouring' is 'thou strivest'
NG is short for no good

explanation.surface: Artists striving to wrap up some useless underclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art' is the old second-person form of 'are', not painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A string vest is a mesh undershirt, the question mark because it is barely clothing.

clue.text: Jumper for Nellie the Elephant — or where she performed?

definitions.meaning: a jumper is a top, and an elephant's would be a large one
the circus tent, which Nellie left in the children's song

explanation.walkthrough: 'Nellie the Elephant' is a British children's song about a circus elephant who packs her trunk and leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A big top is the main tent of a circus; read literally, a large jumper.

clue.text: Vacuous telly guide introduced faux-archaic writing

indicators.note: introduced means the second piece is put inside the first
vacuous means emptied, so only the outside letters of telly remain

parts.note: an usher guides people to their seats

explanation.surface: An empty-headed television guide brought in some mock-old prose.
explanation.definitionFit: Tushery is a word for affected, pseudo-antique literary style full of 'tush' and 'forsooth'.

clue.text: Get a bunch of singers heard

indicators.note: heard says the words are what is spoken, not what is written

parts.note: a choir is a group of singers

explanation.surface: Fetch a group of vocalists that can be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire something is to obtain it.

clue.text: Charge up when infiltrating Italian province

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the whole is read from the bottom
infiltrating means the second piece enters the first

parts.note: Lucca is a province of Tuscany
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A charge arises when an Italian region is infiltrated.
explanation.definitionFit: An accusal is an accusation, a formal charge.

clue.text: Characteristic of drunk entering wharf

indicators.note: entering means the second piece goes into the first

parts.note: a quay is a wharf
lit is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: Typical of a drunkard staggering onto the dock.
explanation.definitionFit: A quality is a distinctive attribute or characteristic.

clue.text: Clown and king go off

parts.note: Feste is the clown in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night
R, rex, is Latin for king

explanation.surface: A jester and a monarch set out together.
explanation.definitionFit: To fester is to rot or putrefy, as food does when it goes off.

clue.text: Frost over, having dined in state

indicators.note: over means the word is turned upwards in this down entry

parts.note: rime is hoar frost
ate is the past of eat

explanation.surface: Frost lies over a country after dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: An emirate is a state ruled by an emir.

clue.text: Fickle Charlie Clark ingesting drug?

parts.note: Charlie Chan is a fictional detective

indicators.note: ingesting means the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: Clark Gable was a Hollywood film star
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: An inconstant man called Charlie Clark taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charlie' and 'Clark' are first names whose famous surnames are wanted, not C from the phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something changeable alters easily, just as a fickle person does.

clue.text: Prejudice results in Indian master going back gutted

indicators.note: gutted means the middle letter is taken out
going back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: sahib was a term of respect for a master in colonial India

explanation.surface: Bigotry comes from a colonial master returning in disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: SAHIB reversed is BIHAS, and 'gutted' removes its central H; 'results in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bias is a one-sided leaning, the same thing as prejudice.

clue.text: House of ill repute is agitated

definitions.meaning: an old word for a brothel

explanation.definitionFit: Stews is an old word for a brothel, and someone who stews frets anxiously.

clue.text: Overeat? Almost turned to drink

indicators.note: turned means the letters are read in reverse order
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to gorge is to overeat

explanation.surface: Stuffing oneself nearly turns to drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Grog is rum diluted with water, or alcoholic drink generally.

clue.text: Use electronic device to commit theft

definitions.meaning: to pass a card through a reader

explanation.definitionFit: To swipe is both to run a card through a reader and, informally, to steal.

clue.text: Get legless — could result be inertia?

indicators.note: could result says the letters of be and inertia might be rearranged to produce something else

explanation.surface: A drinker asks whether slumping into stupor is just inertia.
explanation.definitionFit: To inebriate is to make drunk; legless is British slang for very drunk.

clue.text: Still wearing dead baby's outfit

indicators.note: wearing means the first piece has the second on inside it

parts.note: the late person is someone who has died
yet means still, as in 'not yet'

explanation.surface: A dead infant still dressed in its clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A layette is a complete set of clothes and linen for a newborn.

clue.text: Stray soldier returning in women's clothing

indicators.note: in means the second piece is placed inside the first

parts.note: a dress is a woman's garment

indicators.note: returning means the word is read backwards

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier comes back dressed as a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To digress is to wander from the subject, to stray.
